Issued at 550 PM CDT Sun Aug 30 2026

Tonight: Scattered Showers and Storms Linger

Anvil shading from convection across Iowa kept the lower
troposphere from mixing as efficiently as initially progged
earlier today. This resulted in not only cooler temperatures,
but a larger pool of MUCAPE for convection to realize this 
afternoon and overnight as the LLJ increases after 03-06Z. We 
saw widespread convection develop during the mid-afternoon over 
northeastern Iowa that the short-term guidance essentially fell 
flat on their face in predicting. Only the RAP, with its 
shallower BL depths, has caught onto current trends and was 
used heavily as guidance into the overnight. It develops 
scattered to even widespread convection along the nose of the 
LLJ along and east of the Mississippi River early tonight that 
festers for much of the night as the jet shifts eastward.

With the line parallel steering flow, repeated rounds of storms
could impact the same area. It is not out of the realm of 
possibilities that we see localized pockets of 1-2" of rain 
(<10% chance at a given location), but the drier sub-cloud 
depths may help limit the efficiency of the rainfall rates. 
These showers and storms should exit the local area by sunrise 
as the LLJ weakens and pivots to the east.

Monday - Tuesday: Storm Chances and Increasing Heat

The warm front begins to lift northward Monday morning as a 
closed upper low across southern Canada moves into the region 
bringing a surface trough into the Upper Midwest. Additional 
shower/storm potential exists along this boundary for Monday 
afternoon though confidence is pretty low regarding 
timing/location given the sporadic coverage depicted in the CAM 
solutions, likely influenced by the fair degree of capping 
across the region. The environment does appear to be conducive 
to storm development, some possibly strong to severe, given 
MUCAPE upwards of 2000-3000 J/kg and effective shear of 35-40kts
depicted in model soundings although this potential is highly 
dependent on if storms can get past the cap. Probabilities for 
storms developing sit around 10-20%, highest along/south of 
Highway 18 where forcing along the surface trough will be 
strongest, though recent CAM solutions are beginning to indicate
development may occur north of I-90 where capping is slightly 
weaker. If storms do develop, gusty winds and hail will be the 
main concerns. 

Apart from shower and storm potential, Monday looks to be a hot
day as the persistent warm advection and southerly winds result
in surface temperatures in the mid to upper 80s and dewpoints 
in the upper 60s to low 70s. While cloudiness associated with 
the various waves may act to moderate temperatures slightly, 
ensemble guidance is in fairly good agreement with the warm 
temperatures with the 30.12z HREF suggesting an 60-90% chance 
for highs to exceed 85 degrees area wide. Given the warm 
temperatures and high dewpoints, heat indices Monday afternoon 
are expected to climb into the mid 90s, potentially near 100 
degrees within the river valleys. 

The wave train continues Tuesday as a weak shortwave trough at 
500hPa lifts northward out of the central Great Plains atop a 
developing stationary boundary at the surface. This set-up may lead 
to some additional showers and storms late Tuesday (20-30%) though 
greater chances come early Wednesday morning. Heat also continues 
Tuesday with highs in the upper 80s to around 90 degrees again, 
resulting in heat indices in the mid to upper 90s, warmest south of 
I-90.

Wednesday - Friday: Potential for Showers, Storms, and Warmth 
Continues 

Shower and storm potential continues through the mid to late 
week as the active upper level pattern remains in place. As 
previously noted, Wednesday morning has the highest agreement 
regarding precipitation amongst the 30.00z LREF members as 
another 500hPa shortwave traverses the surface warm front. 
Current probabilities of precipitation sit around 40-70% in the 
LREF grand ensemble and 40-60% in the 30.07z NBM, highest along
and north of I-90 at this point. A greater spread amongst the 
ensemble membership exists past Wednesday, though daily chances 
for showers and storms exist ranging from 20-50% per the 30.07z 
NBM. 

Apart from precipitation chances, continued bouts of warm 
advection associated with predominantly southerly low level 
winds should keep high temperatures around the mid 80s, which is
depicted in the 30.06z ENS/GEFS/GEPS interquartile range. 
Depending on how the potential continuous barrage of rain plays
out, the forecast may ultimately trend towards a warmer or 
cooler solution as the aforementioned divergence of the ensemble
membership does have outliers ranging from the low 90s to upper
70s. Would tend towards the cooler side given the potential 
cloudiness and rainfall, but there's still plenty of time for 
the trend to make itself known.
